governance_authority: Safety Backfire AI Provenance Assurance Committee

corrections.reason: Over-generalization of dataset-level synthetic description to real-world test scenes Warehouse_026 and Warehouse_027
corrections.old_claim: The dataset is synthetically generated with Omniverse and Cosmos Transfer across all warehouse scenes, including Warehouse_026 and Warehouse_027.
corrections.corrected_claim: The NVIDIA PhysicalAI-SmartSpaces benchmark contains mixed provenance, including synthetic scenes and the real-world Warehouse_026 and Warehouse_027 test captures released on 2026-06-04.
corrections.source: NVIDIA PhysicalAI-SmartSpaces Dataset Card and 2026-06-04 Release Changelog
corrections.verification_method: Cross-verification with official dataset card documentation and release changelog

corrections.reason: Inaccurate attribution of independent physical surveying to benchmark-supplied camera calibration without verifiable field surveying records
corrections.old_claim: Two authentic, independently surveyed warehouse facilities provided by NVIDIA PhysicalAI-SmartSpaces benchmark.
corrections.corrected_claim: Two real-world warehouse test captures (Warehouse_026 and Warehouse_027) provided by NVIDIA PhysicalAI-SmartSpaces benchmark. The available project evidence does not independently establish the physical surveying methodology or field measurement uncertainty underlying the supplied calibration.
corrections.verification_method: Artifact inspection confirming calibration is dataset-provided without independent survey logs

corrections.reason: Unjustified empirical generalization of camera pitch depression angles from 11 benchmark cameras to all industrial warehouses worldwide
corrections.old_claim: The canonical top-down assumption is empirically refuted by real-world warehouse deployments; in authentic logistics facilities, cameras are always mounted at shallow angles (20° to 35°).
corrections.corrected_claim: Across the 11 cameras analyzed in Warehouse_026 and Warehouse_027, the optical-axis depression angles derived from the supplied calibration were within the observed range of 20.56°–35.69°. This observation is limited to the two benchmark scenes and must not be generalized to industrial warehouses as a whole.
corrections.verification_method: Sample-size scope constraint verification (N=11 cameras across 2 scenes)

corrections.reason: Improper use of legal/regulatory terms and accusation of 'scientific fraud' in internal technical reports
corrections.old_claim: Generating precision or recall against model predictions would constitute scientific fraud.
corrections.corrected_claim: Generating precision or recall against model predictions would constitute scientifically invalid self-validation (or methodologically invalid ground-truth substitution) because ground truth is withheld by NVIDIA.
corrections.source: Safety Case and Regulatory Terminology Standard (ISO 3691-4, ASME V&V 40)
corrections.verification_method: Terminology audit against engineering assurance guidelines

corrections.reason: Clarification of Model H formal coverage status and distinction between missing physical lux and synthetic failure
corrections.old_claim: Model H failed or cannot be evaluated because the benchmark is synthetic.
corrections.corrected_claim: Model H formal coverage remains unestablished because physical lux telemetry required by the illumination-dependent component is unavailable in the released test capture package. Model H parameters remain strictly frozen (k0=2.40, beta_d=0.08, beta_l=0.12, beta_pitch=0.22).
corrections.source: Model H Lineage Specification and Baseline Lock
corrections.verification_method: Mathematical inspection of Model H formulation and sensor requirements
